actors.title: ATS vendor
actors.content:
# ATS vendor

The platform the funnel runs inside. Writes no policy and decides no hire, yet its defaults decide what a great many people ever see.
actors.summary: The platform the funnel runs inside. Writes no policy and decides no hire, yet its defaults decide what a great many people ever see.
controls: What the parser can extract, and what it silently drops
Which knockout rules a customer can configure, and which are on by default
What the ranking model reads as a feature
When an unreviewed application expires, and what it emails when it does
blind_to: Whether a rule its customer configured is lawful, reasonable or even intended
What happened to a candidate outside the platform
Whether the profile it scored 12/100 was unreadable rather than unqualified
incentives: Throughput and customer-visible efficiency, which are what the buyer evaluates
Feature parity with competitors, including features with known disparate effects
Defaults that reduce customer support load, not candidate confusion

specimens.label: A default nobody chose

lines.text: Setting: auto_expire_unreviewed · Default: enabled · Threshold: 60 days
Setting: employment_gap_penalty · Default: enabled
Both ship on. Turning them off is a customer action nobody is prompted to take.

specimens.reading: Two lines of default configuration account for several mechanisms in this registry and one of its three reinforcing loops.

actors.title: Candidate
actors.content:
# Candidate

The person applying. The only party in the funnel who sees the whole of their own process and almost none of anyone else's.
actors.summary: The person applying. The only party in the funnel who sees the whole of their own process and almost none of anyone else's.
controls: What is submitted, and in what machine-readable shape
Which processes to enter and when to withdraw
Which questions to ask, and when to ask them
What is recorded: dates, wording, who said it
blind_to: Whether a requisition is funded, frozen or already promised internally
The band, the level, and the rubric being scored against
How many others are in the pipeline and where they came from
Whether a rejection was written by a person or emitted by a rule
incentives: Reach a decision quickly enough to keep options open
Avoid spending unpaid hours on processes that were never live
Preserve the ability to reapply without having burned the relationship

specimens.label: What the candidate can and cannot see

lines.text: Visible: every message received, every date, every stated reason, every hour spent.
Invisible: the requisition status, the approved band, the rubric, the queue depth, and whether a human read anything.
Most of the pain of a hiring process is an attempt to infer the second list from the first.

specimens.reading: This asymmetry is the reason the registry exists. It does not remove it — it makes the boundary between the two lists explicit.

actors.title: Employer policy
actors.content:
# Employer policy

Finance, leadership and the people function: the layer that authorises headcount, fixes bands and writes the rules the funnel executes. Never meets a candidate.
actors.summary: Finance, leadership and the people function: the layer that authorises headcount, fixes bands and writes the rules the funnel executes. Never meets a candidate.
controls: Whether a requisition is funded, and whether it stays funded
The band and the levelling grid
Whether postings must be published externally regardless of internal candidates
What may be disclosed, and what must not be
blind_to: What a freeze looks like from the far end of a five-round process
How a compliance posting reads to someone who spent six weeks on it
The cumulative candidate hours a policy consumes
incentives: Optionality: an approved requisition that can be paused costs less than one that cannot
Consistency and legal defensibility across every hire
Cost control, on a cycle measured in quarters rather than in conversations

specimens.label: Where the decisions actually sit

lines.text: Requisition funded: finance · Band: compensation · Level: levelling committee
External posting required regardless of an internal candidate: policy
Interviews conducted: the team. Rejection sent: the recruiter.
The candidate only ever meets the last two rows.

specimens.reading: Several observations in this registry are the visible end of a decision taken in a row the candidate never sees.

actors.title: Hiring manager
actors.content:
# Hiring manager

The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
actors.summary: The person the role reports to, and the panel they convene. Sets the bar, owns the outcome, and is doing this alongside the work the role exists to absorb.
controls: The requirements as written, and the ones only they know about
Who interviews and what they ask
The level a candidate is assessed at
Whether a split panel becomes a hire
blind_to: What the same candidate showed in rounds they did not attend
How the requirements read to someone outside the team
What the search is costing the people covering the gap
incentives: Avoid a bad hire, which is visible and attributed, more than a missed hire, which is neither
Fill the gap without the ramp-up cost of someone who needs teaching
Keep the team's own delivery on track while running the loop

specimens.label: The asymmetry that sets the bar

lines.text: A bad hire is visible for a year and attributed to the person who made it.
A missed hire is invisible and attributed to nobody.
Both are costly. Only one has a name on it.

specimens.reading: This is not a bias to be scolded out of anyone; it is an incentive with a shape. Several conservative-default mechanisms follow from it directly.

actors.title: Public policy and industry standards
actors.content:
# Public policy and industry standards

Regulators, labour law, and the conventions the market copies from itself. Sets the outer bounds and moves on a timescale no individual process can wait for.
actors.summary: Regulators, labour law, and the conventions the market copies from itself. Sets the outer bounds and moves on a timescale no individual process can wait for.
controls: What must be disclosed — pay transparency rules being the clearest current example
What automated decision-making is permitted, and what must be explainable
Which employment relationships are possible in which jurisdiction
blind_to: How a rule is implemented once it reaches a configuration screen
Practices that are legal, ordinary, and still produce the effects catalogued here
incentives: Rules that are enforceable and measurable, which is a narrower set than rules that would help
Not disrupting labour markets faster than they can absorb the change

specimens.label: What a disclosure rule reaches, and what it does not

lines.text: Covered by pay transparency rules: the band must appear in the posting.
Not covered: at which level the candidate will actually be assessed.
Not covered: whether the requisition is funded, or already promised internally.

specimens.reading: The strongest external lever in this registry closes one branch of the compensation bind and leaves the levelling branch entirely open.

actors.title: Recruiter
actors.content:
# Recruiter

The function that moves people through the funnel. Holds the most information about the process and the least authority over its outcome.
actors.summary: The function that moves people through the funnel. Holds the most information about the process and the least authority over its outcome.
controls: Which applications are read and in what order
What is disclosed at the screen, and when
The wording of the rejection
Whether a candidate is told a search has stalled
blind_to: What the panel actually scored, beyond the recommendation
Whether finance will approve the headcount this quarter
What the hiring manager privately requires but has not written down
incentives: Move the pipeline; time-to-fill is measured, time-to-clarity is not
Protect the relationship with the hiring manager, who is the internal client
Avoid saying anything that could be quoted back as a commitment

specimens.label: The week as the metrics see it

lines.text: Open requisitions: 11 · Applications received: 640 · Screening capacity: 40
Measured: time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, offer acceptance.
Not measured: time-to-clarity, or whether anyone who was rejected understood why.

specimens.reading: Several mechanisms in this registry are the shape of this table rather than of any decision anyone made.

workflows.title: The hiring funnel, end to end
workflows.content:
# The hiring funnel, end to end

From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
workflows.summary: From the moment headcount is authorised to a signed contract or a closed search, with the actor who owns each step and what the candidate can see from where they stand.
workflows.subject: a requisition and the candidate moving through it

states.title: Requisition drafted
states.description: A manager writes the role. Level, band and requirements are decided here, usually by copying the last search for the same team.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing. The role does not exist publicly yet.

states.title: Headcount authorised
states.description: Finance and leadership commit budget against the requisition. Approval can lapse or be withdrawn later without the funnel noticing.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Posting live
states.description: The role is public. It may also be refreshed automatically every thirty days, which looks identical to a new opening.
states.visible_to_candidate: The posting, and whatever the posting chose to disclose.

states.title: Application received
states.description: A record exists and is linked to the requisition. Nothing has been read.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation, or silence.

states.title: Automated screen
states.description: Parser extraction, keyword thresholds, knockout rules and ranking. Decided in under a second.
states.visible_to_candidate: Either nothing, or a rejection within minutes.

states.title: In the recruiter queue
states.description: Waiting to be read by a person, against an inbound queue that is usually larger than the week has hours for.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, of an indeterminate length.

states.title: Recruiter screen
states.description: A conversation about compensation, timeline, location and a two-minute version of the last project.
states.visible_to_candidate: The call itself, and whichever parameters the recruiter chose to share.

states.title: Technical assessment
states.description: A live exercise, a take-home, or both, scored against a rubric the candidate does not see.
states.visible_to_candidate: The exercise, and sometimes structured feedback afterwards.

states.title: Manager and team panel
states.description: Depth, ownership and collaboration, assessed across several interviewers who may be measuring different things.
states.visible_to_candidate: The conversations. Rarely the scores.

states.title: Compensation and levelling
states.description: The level the panel assigned meets the band finance approved. First time the two are compared.
states.visible_to_candidate: A number, or a renegotiation.

states.title: Offer approval
states.description: Manager, director, finance and the talent committee sign off in sequence. Everyone the candidate met has already said yes.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, usually described as "final checks".

states.title: Offer issued
states.description: A written offer exists. The requisition is still open until the countersignature lands.
states.visible_to_candidate: The offer document.

states.title: Reference and background check
states.description: A third-party record is compared against what the candidate claimed.
states.visible_to_candidate: A request for documents, or nothing.

states.title: Hired
states.description: Contract executed both ways, start date set, onboarding triggered.
states.visible_to_candidate: A signed contract.

states.title: Rejected
states.description: A decision was made and communicated. What it says about the cause is a separate question entirely.
states.visible_to_candidate: A message, ranging from a rubric category to a template.

states.title: Search frozen or cancelled
states.description: Budget withdrawn or the requisition put on hold. Can happen at any point, including after an offer.
states.visible_to_candidate: If the candidate is lucky, an explanation. Often the posting simply disappears.

states.title: Lapsed without a decision
states.description: No one decided anything. The record aged past a threshold, or the posting was never taken down.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence, then possibly a bulk rejection at two in the morning.

transitions.label: budget signed off
transitions.guard: Finance commits headcount against the requisition.

transitions.label: posting goes live
transitions.guard: An approved requisition with a written description is published.

transitions.label: application submitted
transitions.guard: The candidate applies, or answers outbound outreach.

transitions.label: rules evaluated
transitions.guard: The record is complete enough for the configured rules to run.

transitions.label: thresholds cleared
transitions.guard: Extraction score and every knockout rule pass.

transitions.label: filtered out
transitions.guard: Any knockout rule fails, or the ranking falls below the advance threshold.

transitions.label: short-listed
transitions.guard: A person reads the profile and puts it on the list.

transitions.label: aged out
transitions.guard: No review happened before the expiry threshold.

transitions.label: parameters align
transitions.guard: Expectations, timeline and location are compatible, and the profile is submitted to the team.

transitions.label: parameters do not align
transitions.guard: Compensation, level, location or availability rules the candidate out before any engineering is discussed.

transitions.label: assessment passed
transitions.guard: The score clears the rubric threshold.

transitions.label: assessment not passed
transitions.guard: The score falls short, or the review was too shallow to find what was there.

transitions.label: panel recommends hire
transitions.guard: Consensus reaches the hire threshold.

transitions.label: panel does not reach consensus
transitions.guard: A split panel under a unanimity rule defaults to no hire.

transitions.label: level and band reconcile
transitions.guard: The assigned level and the approved band overlap.

transitions.label: level and band do not reconcile
transitions.guard: Expectation sits outside the band and neither the level nor the number moves.

transitions.label: sign-off complete
transitions.guard: Every approver in the chain has cleared it.

transitions.label: headcount withdrawn
transitions.guard: Budget is pulled or a freeze is announced before the offer is issued.

transitions.label: offer accepted
transitions.guard: The candidate signs and the checks begin.

transitions.label: offer retracted
transitions.guard: A freeze reaches an outstanding offer before the countersignature.

transitions.label: checks clear
transitions.guard: No unresolved discrepancy in the third-party record.

transitions.label: discrepancy unresolved
transitions.guard: A record mismatch or an eligibility bar is not reconciled.

transitions.label: posting outlives the search
transitions.guard: Hiring stops but the listing is never withdrawn.

transitions.label: requisition reopened
transitions.guard: The search restarts, sometimes with a revised profile, sometimes as an automatic refresh.

workflows.title: An application inside the ATS
workflows.content:
# An application inside the ATS

The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
workflows.summary: The machine the candidate never sees: what happens to a submitted application between the form and a human being, and the four ways it can end without anyone reading it.
workflows.subject: one application record

states.title: Submitted
states.description: A form post has been accepted. Fields are validated against the requisition schema; nothing has been interpreted.
states.visible_to_candidate: A confirmation page, sometimes an acknowledgement email.

states.title: Parsing
states.description: The document is converted to structured fields. Multi-column layouts, graphics and custom fonts routinely lose whole sections silently.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing.

states.title: Rule evaluation
states.description: Knockout rules, keyword coverage, years thresholds and ranking features run in sequence, short-circuiting on the first failure.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing, for a second or two.

states.title: Queued for human review
states.description: The record is above the threshold and waiting. Queue position depends on source: outbound lists are usually read first.
states.visible_to_candidate: Silence. This is where most of the waiting happens.

states.title: Read by a person
states.description: A recruiter opens the profile. The median attention available per profile is measured in seconds when the queue is deep.
states.visible_to_candidate: Nothing yet.

states.title: Advanced to the funnel
states.description: The record leaves this machine and enters WF-001 at the recruiter screen.
states.visible_to_candidate: An invitation to talk.

states.title: Rejected by rule
states.description: A rule failed. The notification is often queued and sent minutes later, which is what produces a rejection at midnight.
states.visible_to_candidate: A rejection email, minutes after applying.

states.title: Rejected by a person
states.description: Someone read it and passed. What the message says about why is a separate decision, usually a template.
states.visible_to_candidate: A rejection message, generic unless a feedback policy exists.

states.title: Expired unreviewed
states.description: A scheduled job closed the record after a threshold. Nobody read it, and the email it sends is indistinguishable from one that followed a review.
states.visible_to_candidate: A bulk rejection, or nothing at all.

transitions.label: document accepted
transitions.guard: Required fields validate and the file is a supported type.

transitions.label: fields extracted
transitions.guard: Extraction completes, whether or not it recovered the work history.

transitions.label: all rules pass
transitions.guard: Every knockout rule passes and the rank clears the advance threshold.

transitions.label: a rule fails
transitions.guard: Any knockout rule fails, or the ranking falls below the threshold.

transitions.label: a recruiter opens it
transitions.guard: Capacity reaches this position in the queue before the expiry threshold.

transitions.label: threshold reached first
transitions.guard: The record ages past the configured limit with no review recorded.

transitions.label: short-listed
transitions.guard: The profile is put on the active list for outreach.

transitions.label: passed over
transitions.guard: The recruiter decides not to advance it.

artifacts.title: Complete silence after submission
artifacts.content:
# Complete silence after submission

No automated receipt, acknowledgement, rejection, or recruiter outreach is received following application submission.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
- Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.
artifacts.summary: No automated receipt, acknowledgement, rejection, or recruiter outreach is received following application submission.

probes.action: Check email spam and security quarantine folders for ATS automated acknowledgement tokens.
probes.expected_signal: Confirms whether application was ingested and generated a confirmation ID.

specimens.label: ATS status history
specimens.context: exported by the candidate on day 41

lines.text: Application received — Senior Backend Engineer
Status: Under review
Status: Under review

specimens.reading: The record shows one state change and then nothing. Silence here is the absence of an event, not an event with a hidden meaning.

specimens.label: Follow-up message to the listed contact

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Hello — I applied for the Senior Backend Engineer role on the 3rd and wanted to check the application went through. Happy to send anything else that helps.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up on the note above. If the search has been paused or filled, that is completely fine — I would just like to close the loop on my side.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: Two polite, dated attempts and no response. What is established is the absence of a reply, not a decision about the candidate.

non_inferences: Does not prove the application was reviewed by a human.
Does not prove the role was cancelled or already filled.

artifacts.title: Generic "closer alignment" rejection template
artifacts.content:
# Generic "closer alignment" rejection template

Standard automated email stating the team decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles more closely match role requirements.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
- Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.
artifacts.summary: Standard automated email stating the team decided to proceed with candidates whose profiles more closely match role requirements.

probes.action: Compare CV keyword density with exact requirement phrases in the published job description.
probes.expected_signal: Reveals potential vocabulary mismatch between candidate phrasing and ATS rubric.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Update on your application

lines.text: Thank you for your interest in our company and for the time you invested in the process.
After careful consideration we have decided to move forward with candidates whose profiles more closely align with the requirements of the role.
We wish you the best in your search and encourage you to apply for future openings.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the text is specific to this candidate, this conversation or this role. The message is a routing decision rendered as prose.

specimens.label: Request for specifics, and the reply

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for letting me know. If it is possible, I would value one line on which requirement was the gap — it would genuinely help me aim better.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Unfortunately we are not able to share individual feedback. It was a very competitive process.

specimens.reading: The follow-up returns the same shape of answer. A template that survives a direct question is a policy, not an opinion about you.

non_inferences: Does not establish which specific skill was deemed insufficient.
Does not establish whether a human reviewer read the full resume.

artifacts.title: Position closed after final interview without hire
artifacts.content:
# Position closed after final interview without hire

Candidate completes all interview rounds, but is informed that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate failed technical or behavioral evaluations.
- Does not prove the company lied about opening intention.
artifacts.summary: Candidate completes all interview rounds, but is informed that the requisition has been cancelled, frozen, or closed.

probes.action: Politely inquire with recruiter if the position was closed due to business budget restructuring or team reallocation.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether barrier was candidate-specific or macroeconomic/budgetary.

specimens.label: Final round, closing minutes
specimens.context: minute 47 of 50, four days before the email below

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: That is everything from our side. Any questions for us?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Only about timing — what happens next?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: We are wrapping up the loop this week. You are the last of three finalists, so expect to hear back by Friday at the latest.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Thank you for the time.

specimens.reading: The process was described as live and near a decision. Whatever happened next happened after this point, not before it.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Regarding the Senior Backend Engineer search

lines.text: Thank you again for the conversations over the past six weeks — the panel was consistently positive about your work.
I am writing with disappointing news: the requisition has been put on hold as part of a wider planning review, and we will not be filling the role this quarter.
This is not a reflection on your interviews. If the role reopens I would like to come back to you first.

specimens.reading: The stated cause sits above the hiring loop entirely. A candidate cannot pass or fail a budget review.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate failed technical or behavioral evaluations.
Does not prove the company lied about opening intention.

artifacts.title: Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection
artifacts.content:
# Materially similar role reposted shortly after rejection

Candidate observes the same or near-identical job listing reposted or refreshed on job boards within 1–8 weeks of rejection.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
- Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.
artifacts.summary: Candidate observes the same or near-identical job listing reposted or refreshed on job boards within 1–8 weeks of rejection.

probes.action: Check job listing requisition ID or ask recruiter whether the posting is an automated ATS refresh or a distinct headcount opening.
probes.expected_signal: Distinguishes between automated job board bot refreshes and genuine recurring hiring demand.

specimens.label: The two postings, side by side
specimens.context: rejection on 14 March, repost seen on 2 April

lines.text: 14 Mar — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
2 Apr — Senior Backend Engineer · Payments · Remote (EU) · 5+ years · Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka · req #4471
Body text identical except for the posted date. Same requisition number, same team, same band.

specimens.reading: The requisition number is the thing to record. A refreshed listing and a genuinely new headcount look identical on the board and are different facts underneath.

specimens.label: Asking the recruiter directly

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 posted again this week. Is this a second opening on the team, or the same one refreshed?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Good catch — the board auto-refreshes listings after 30 days so they stay visible. Same requisition, still open.

specimens.reading: One question separated an automated refresh from a real second opening. This is the cheapest probe in the whole registry.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the role was a "fake" or "ghost" posting.
Does not establish that the prior interview feedback was fraudulent.

artifacts.title: Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process
artifacts.content:
# Compensation band reduced or altered mid-process

Offered or discussed compensation band is revised downward from previously agreed or advertised range.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove intentional bait-and-switch malice unless verified by company policy evidence.
artifacts.summary: Offered or discussed compensation band is revised downward from previously agreed or advertised range.

probes.action: Request clarification on whether the revised band reflects a lower leveling grade or a company-wide budget adjustment.
probes.expected_signal: Separates leveling evaluation outcome from company financial constraints.

specimens.label: Recruiter message before the offer call

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Quick heads-up before we talk numbers tomorrow — where did we land on expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Same as the range in the posting and what we agreed at the screen: 85–95k.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. So finance has revised the band for this level since we opened the role. We are working with 72–78k now.

specimens.reading: The number moved after the candidate had already spent the process. Note the date the original band was stated and by whom.

specimens.label: Offer call, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Was the change specific to me, or to the level?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: To the level. Everyone coming in at this grade this quarter is on the new band.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: And the posting still shows the old range?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: It does. I will get that updated.

specimens.reading: An answer that generalises to the whole grade describes a policy. An answer that is specific to you would describe an assessment. They are different mechanisms.

non_inferences: Does not prove intentional bait-and-switch malice unless verified by company policy evidence.

artifacts.title: Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope
artifacts.content:
# Take-home assignment exceeding reasonable stated scope

Take-home assignment requires building complex production-grade features demanding 20+ hours instead of stated 2–4 hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.
artifacts.summary: Take-home assignment requires building complex production-grade features demanding 20+ hours instead of stated 2–4 hours.

probes.action: Define explicit boundaries and trade-offs in submission README stating assumptions made to fit the agreed timebox.
probes.expected_signal: Tests whether evaluators value scope management and communication over unbounded free work.

specimens.label: The assignment brief, as received
specimens.subject: Take-home exercise — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Build a service that ingests order events, deduplicates them, and exposes a query API over the resulting state.

Requirements: persistence with migrations, idempotent consumers, retry with backoff, structured logging, metrics endpoint, containerised local run, integration tests, and a short design document covering scaling and failure modes.
Please submit within one week. We estimate 2–4 hours.

specimens.reading: Count the deliverables against the stated budget. The mismatch is measurable, which makes it a fact rather than a feeling.

specimens.label: Asking about scope

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to do this. To fit the 2–4 hours, which parts should I treat as the core and which can I stub with a note in the README?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Ideally all of it — we use it to see how you work end to end.

specimens.reading: The stated budget and the expected deliverable are not reconciled when asked directly. That is the observation; the reason for it is not visible from here.

non_inferences: Does not prove the company is harvesting free intellectual property for production use.

artifacts.title: Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show
artifacts.content:
# Multiple interview reschedulings or interviewer no-show

Interviews are repeatedly postponed, delayed at short notice, or interviewer fails to join scheduled call.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.
artifacts.summary: Interviews are repeatedly postponed, delayed at short notice, or interviewer fails to join scheduled call.

probes.action: Offer clear flexible availability slots and confirm contact details 2 hours prior to the call.
probes.expected_signal: Minimizes scheduling friction and verifies recruiter responsiveness.

specimens.label: Scheduling thread

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Tuesday 14:00 works for the panel — sending the invite now.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Apologies, the interviewer has a conflict. Can we move to Thursday same time?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Sorry to do this again — Thursday is out. Would Monday work?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Something urgent came up on the team. I will come back to you with new slots.

specimens.reading: Four movements, no interview. Record the dates: a pattern of postponement is evidence about the process, not about the candidate.

specimens.label: Calendar record

lines.text: Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser
Invite sent — Technical panel
Cancelled by organiser · no replacement issued

specimens.reading: Every cancellation came from the same side. That asymmetry is the observable part.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate rejection; frequently reflects interviewer calendar congestion or emergency incidents.

artifacts.title: Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall
artifacts.content:
# Explicit feedback citing skill-depth shortfall

Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply general incompetence; reflects threshold for this specific role level.
artifacts.summary: Interviewer or recruiter provides structured notes citing a specific deficit in algorithmic complexity, architecture, or tool mastery.

probes.action: Review interview problem solution against industry standard patterns and identify edge cases missed.
probes.expected_signal: Verifies whether candidate code truly lacked required optimization or rigor.

specimens.label: Structured feedback notes
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical panel

lines.text: The panel was positive on system decomposition and on how you reasoned about failure modes.

The gap was in the second exercise: the solution was correct but quadratic, and the panel was looking for the linear approach using a hash index. We would want to see that reached without prompting at this level.
We are not moving forward now, but this was close and we would welcome a re-application in six months.

specimens.reading: A named exercise, a named property, a named expectation. This is the rare rejection that is actually actionable.

specimens.label: The moment in the panel

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: This works. What is the complexity?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Quadratic — nested scan over the same list.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Right. Can you get it down?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Probably with an index of some kind. I would want to think about it.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: That is fine, let us move on for time.

specimens.reading: The transcript and the written feedback agree. When they agree, the feedback is describing something that actually happened.

non_inferences: Does not imply general incompetence; reflects threshold for this specific role level.

artifacts.title: Rejection within minutes of application submission
artifacts.content:
# Rejection within minutes of application submission

Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside human business hours.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate resume was judged as poor by human engineers.
artifacts.summary: Automated rejection email arrives within 2 to 30 minutes of form submission, outside human business hours.

probes.action: Audit application answers to mandatory knock-out questions (work permit, country of residence, minimum years experience).
probes.expected_signal: Identifies exact boolean filter rule triggered by ATS.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application

lines.text: Thank you for applying. After reviewing your application we have decided not to proceed at this time.
Sent 23:58 — eleven minutes after submission, outside working hours in every timezone the company operates in.

specimens.reading: The interval is the evidence. Eleven minutes at midnight describes the throughput of a rule, not the attention of a reader.

specimens.label: Application timeline

lines.text: Application submitted
Screening rules evaluated
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria
Notification email queued

specimens.reading: Two seconds between submission and decision. The eleven-minute delay was the mail queue, not deliberation.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate resume was judged as poor by human engineers.

artifacts.title: Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel
artifacts.content:
# Communication mismatch or tone friction in panel

Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate lacks teamwork skills globally.
artifacts.summary: Noticeable divergence in communication style, pacing, or terminology during live panel discussions.

probes.action: Request explicit feedback on collaborative dynamic from recruiter.
probes.expected_signal: Clarifies whether friction was perceived as attitude issue or stylistic preference.

specimens.label: Panel discussion, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: So when you say the write path is eventually consistent, what does the client see?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Depends on the read. If it goes through the cache it can be stale by up to the TTL; if it goes to the primary it is current.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: Sorry, I think we are talking past each other. I meant from the user perspective.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Ah — then: they may see their own write missing for a second or two.

lines.speaker: Interviewer A
lines.text: That is what I was after.

specimens.reading: The disagreement was about which layer the question lived in, not about the answer. The content was right at both levels.

specimens.label: Panel feedback
specimens.subject: Feedback — architecture round

lines.text: Technically solid throughout.
The panel felt communication was not always calibrated to the audience — answers went to implementation detail where a product-level framing was wanted.

specimens.reading: Read against the transcript this is one exchange generalised into a trait. Both readings fit the same recording, which is exactly why the observation is not a verdict.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate lacks teamwork skills globally.

artifacts.title: Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze
artifacts.content:
# Offer rescinded or delayed due to internal freeze

Candidate is verbally offered a role or receives written offer which is subsequently delayed or retracted before start date.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply candidate failed reference checks unless explicitly stated.
artifacts.summary: Candidate is verbally offered a role or receives written offer which is subsequently delayed or retracted before start date.

probes.action: Request formal written notice regarding whether requisition is permanently cancelled or deferred to next fiscal quarter.
probes.expected_signal: Provides timeline clarity for candidate decision-making.

specimens.label: The offer, then the retraction
specimens.subject: Offer — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Day 0 — Delighted to confirm the offer we discussed. Start date 1 June, contract attached for signature.
Day 9 — I am very sorry to write this. A company-wide hiring freeze was announced this morning and all outstanding offers are suspended, including yours.
Day 9 — I understand you may have given notice. Please tell me if there is anything I can do, and I will be honest with you about what I can and cannot influence.

specimens.reading: Two dated documents about the same role. Whatever happens next, the fact that a written offer existed on day 0 is established, not remembered.

specimens.label: Establishing the scope of the freeze

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is the freeze specific to the team, or company-wide?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Company-wide. Every open req is paused, and three other offers are in the same position as yours.

specimens.reading: The answer places the cause outside the hiring loop and outside the candidate. It also makes the claim checkable against public news.

non_inferences: Does not imply candidate failed reference checks unless explicitly stated.

artifacts.title: Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting
artifacts.content:
# Unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by ghosting

Recruiter initiates direct outreach expressing strong interest, but ceases communication after candidate responds with availability.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove candidate profile was rejected; often indicates batch automated sourcing campaigns.
artifacts.summary: Recruiter initiates direct outreach expressing strong interest, but ceases communication after candidate responds with availability.

probes.action: Send one single polite follow-up after 5 business days referencing original outreach thread.
probes.expected_signal: Recovers stalled conversation if recruiter was out-of-office or overwhelmed.

specimens.label: Inbound outreach, then silence

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Hi! I came across your profile — your work on payment infrastructure is exactly what our team needs. Would you be open to a chat this week?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Thanks for reaching out. Yes, happy to talk. I am free Tuesday or Thursday after 15:00, and here is a short summary of what I have been working on.
— no reply —

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Following up in case this got buried. Still interested.
— no reply —

specimens.reading: The enthusiasm and the disappearance came from the same side, and the candidate did nothing between them except answer.

specimens.label: What was and was not established

lines.text: Established: an outreach message was sent on day 0; the candidate replied the same day with availability; two follow-ups went unanswered over eleven days.
Not established: whether the role existed, whether it was filled, whether anyone read the reply, or what the recruiter thought of the profile.

specimens.reading: Writing the two lists separately is the whole method. Most of the pain of this signal comes from filling the second list with guesses.

non_inferences: Does not prove candidate profile was rejected; often indicates batch automated sourcing campaigns.

artifacts.title: Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade
artifacts.content:
# Feedback stating candidate is overqualified for the grade

Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope exceeds the open position tier.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not imply the candidate is undesirable, but signals retention/flight-risk and compensation mismatch concerns.
artifacts.summary: Candidate is rejected on the grounds that their experience, seniority, or previous scope exceeds the open position tier.

probes.action: Inquire whether the organization has higher-tier or staff-level requisitions open where broader scope is desired.
probes.expected_signal: Channels candidate into appropriate leveling track.

specimens.label: Rejection email
specimens.subject: Your application — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Thank you for the time you gave us over the past two weeks. The team enjoyed the conversation and rated your systems background highly.

After discussion we have decided not to move forward. Your experience sits above the band we scoped for this role, and we were concerned the day-to-day would not stay interesting for you for very long.
We would be glad to keep your profile on file and reach out when something at the right level opens up.

specimens.reading: The stated ground is fit with a band, not the quality of the work — and the risk named is retention, not capability.

specimens.label: Recruiter screen, transcript fragment

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Your last role was a team lead position, is that right?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Formally, yes. In practice about two thirds of my week was hands-on.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Got it. I will be honest with you — my worry is that this role is a step down, and six months in you would be looking again.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Right now I am optimising for depth rather than scope.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Understood. I will pass that on either way.

specimens.reading: The concern is raised before any technical assessment: the level question is being settled ahead of the skill question.

non_inferences: Does not imply the candidate is undesirable, but signals retention/flight-risk and compensation mismatch concerns.

artifacts.title: Conflicting feedback across different interviewers
artifacts.content:
# Conflicting feedback across different interviewers

Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not prove bad faith; highlights lack of rubric calibration across the hiring committee.
artifacts.summary: Feedback from one round praises architectural depth while another round claims insufficient technical background.

probes.action: Request aggregated hiring rubric summary from talent partner.
probes.expected_signal: Reveals whether team had misaligned internal evaluation criteria.

specimens.label: Two rounds, two verdicts
specimens.subject: Consolidated feedback

lines.text: Round 2 (systems): Strong architectural depth. Reasoned clearly about consistency trade-offs and failure modes. Recommend proceed.
Round 4 (technical): Insufficient depth for the level. Struggled to move past a first-pass solution. Recommend do not proceed.
Final decision: do not proceed.

specimens.reading: Both notes are about the same person in the same week. At least one of them is measuring something other than the candidate.

specimens.label: What the two rounds actually asked

lines.speaker: Interviewer B
lines.text: Round 2 — Walk me through how you would keep two regions in sync when the link between them drops.

lines.speaker: Interviewer D
lines.text: Round 4 — Here is a string parsing problem. You have twenty-five minutes.

specimens.reading: The rounds did not disagree about the candidate; they measured different things and reported both as depth.

non_inferences: Does not prove bad faith; highlights lack of rubric calibration across the hiring committee.

barriers.title: Requisition Approval & Public Posting
barriers.content:
# Requisition Approval & Public Posting

The gate that exists before any candidate does: headcount is authorized, the job description is written, and the requisition is published (or quietly kept open) on careers pages and job boards.

### Pass Condition
An approved requisition with a written job description is published against real, funded headcount.
barriers.description: The gate that exists before any candidate does: headcount is authorized, the job description is written, and the requisition is published (or quietly kept open) on careers pages and job boards.
barriers.pass_condition: An approved requisition with a written job description is published against real, funded headcount.

specimens.label: What was approved before anyone applied

lines.text: Headcount: 1 · Funded from: platform budget, FY approved · Level: L4 · Band: 68–79k
Job description drafted by the hiring manager, edited by recruiting, published unchanged.
Requirements list carried over from the previous L5 search for the same team.

specimens.reading: This gate closes before the first candidate exists, and it fixes the level, the band and the requirements that everyone downstream will be measured against.

barriers.title: Outbound Sourcing & Talent Pool Contact
barriers.content:
# Outbound Sourcing & Talent Pool Contact

Recruiter-initiated outreach to passive candidates and talent-pool building, independent of any inbound application.

### Pass Condition
The candidate responds to outreach and is attached to an active, authorized requisition rather than a speculative pool.
barriers.description: Recruiter-initiated outreach to passive candidates and talent-pool building, independent of any inbound application.
barriers.pass_condition: The candidate responds to outreach and is attached to an active, authorized requisition rather than a speculative pool.

specimens.label: Outreach, and what it was attached to

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Your platform work looks like a strong match for a role we are opening. Open to a conversation?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Yes. Is there an approved requisition behind it?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Not yet approved — we expect sign-off next quarter and want to be ready.

specimens.reading: This gate passes only when outreach is attached to a real, funded requisition. Attached to a forecast, it is a pipeline entry with no gate behind it.

barriers.title: Application Ingestion
barriers.content:
# Application Ingestion

The initial ingestion gate where candidate CV and structured application fields enter the talent acquisition database / ATS.

### Pass Condition
Application record is successfully received, validated for minimum schema, and linked to the active job requisition.
barriers.description: The initial ingestion gate where candidate CV and structured application fields enter the talent acquisition database / ATS.
barriers.pass_condition: Application record is successfully received, validated for minimum schema, and linked to the active job requisition.

specimens.label: What the gate wrote

lines.text: POST /apply — 200 OK
Candidate record created · linked to req #4471
Required fields validated: 12 of 12
Status: Under review

specimens.reading: Passing this gate means a row exists and is attached to a live requisition. It says nothing about whether anyone will read it.

barriers.title: Automated Filter & Parser Threshold
barriers.content:
# Automated Filter & Parser Threshold

Algorithmic text extraction, keyword scoring, compliance screening (location/work authorization), and knockout question evaluations.

### Pass Condition
CV parsing achieves sufficient extraction score and candidate passes all mandatory algorithmic gating rules.
barriers.description: Algorithmic text extraction, keyword scoring, compliance screening (location/work authorization), and knockout question evaluations.
barriers.pass_condition: CV parsing achieves sufficient extraction score and candidate passes all mandatory algorithmic gating rules.

specimens.label: The scoring pass

lines.text: Parser extraction score: 84/100 — PASS
Work authorization question: answered — PASS
Knockout rule years_experience >= 5: candidate 6 — PASS
Keyword coverage: 7 of 9 required terms — PASS (threshold 6)
Advanced to recruiter queue

specimens.reading: Everything at this gate is a threshold on a number. A person who clears it and a person who misses by one term are separated by arithmetic, not by judgement.

barriers.title: Inbound Screening & Triage
barriers.content:
# Inbound Screening & Triage

Recruiter or sourcing coordinator manual review of parsed inbound applications vs active outbound talent pipelines.

### Pass Condition
Recruiter assigns application to the active short-list for initial conversational outreach.
barriers.description: Recruiter or sourcing coordinator manual review of parsed inbound applications vs active outbound talent pipelines.
barriers.pass_condition: Recruiter assigns application to the active short-list for initial conversational outreach.

specimens.label: Triage note, as recorded
specimens.context: one of 40 profiles reviewed that day

lines.text: Source: inbound. Queue position 211 of 640.
Skim: backend, payments, right seniority band. No red flags.
Action: short-list for screen. Note — we are also running an outbound list for this req and those go first.

specimens.reading: Inbound and outbound applications compete at this gate, and they do not arrive on equal footing. Position in the queue is part of the outcome.

barriers.title: Recruiter Screening Call
barriers.content:
# Recruiter Screening Call

Initial conversational interview evaluating salary expectations, timeline, communication, English fluency, and high-level role alignment.

### Pass Condition
Recruiter and candidate align on core parameters and candidate is submitted to hiring team.
barriers.description: Initial conversational interview evaluating salary expectations, timeline, communication, English fluency, and high-level role alignment.
barriers.pass_condition: Recruiter and candidate align on core parameters and candidate is submitted to hiring team.

specimens.label: What this gate actually asks

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: What are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: What is your notice period and earliest start?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Where are you based, and are you authorised to work there?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Give me the two-minute version of your last project.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Any other processes running that we should know about?

specimens.reading: Four of the five questions are logistics and one is technical. This gate mostly filters on parameters, which is why it can end a process before any engineering is discussed.

barriers.title: Technical Screen / Live Assessment
barriers.content:
# Technical Screen / Live Assessment

Synchronous technical evaluation assessing core technical competencies, problem-solving speed, and system architecture fundamentals.

### Pass Condition
Candidate achieves passing score on technical evaluation rubric from the assessing engineer.
barriers.description: Synchronous technical evaluation assessing core technical competencies, problem-solving speed, and system architecture fundamentals.
barriers.pass_condition: Candidate achieves passing score on technical evaluation rubric from the assessing engineer.

specimens.label: The rubric the engineer scored against

lines.text: Correctness: 4/5 · Complexity reasoning: 3/5 · Communication: 4/5 · Testing instinct: 3/5
Threshold to advance: 14/20. Total: 14.
Recommendation: advance, weak yes.

specimens.reading: The gate is a sum against a line. A weak yes and a strong no differ by two points in one column, and the candidate never sees the columns.

barriers.title: Take-Home / Work Sample Evaluation
barriers.content:
# Take-Home / Work Sample Evaluation

Asynchronous technical assignment or project artifact reviewed by engineering peers against quality benchmarks.

### Pass Condition
Code artifact satisfies architectural, functional, test coverage, and documentation requirements.
barriers.description: Asynchronous technical assignment or project artifact reviewed by engineering peers against quality benchmarks.
barriers.pass_condition: Code artifact satisfies architectural, functional, test coverage, and documentation requirements.

specimens.label: Review record

lines.text: Submission received: 41 files, 78 tests, README with design rationale.
Reviewer 1: 9 minutes. Reviewer 2: 4 minutes.
Scored on: architecture, test coverage, documentation, commit hygiene.
Outcome: advance.

specimens.reading: This gate compares hours of work against minutes of review. It can pass or fail on what a reader happened to open.

barriers.title: Hiring Manager In-Depth Review
barriers.content:
# Hiring Manager In-Depth Review

Detailed evaluation of candidate seniority, project ownership history, trade-off reasoning, and team-specific mission fit.

### Pass Condition
Hiring manager confirms candidate has required depth and approves progression to final panel.
barriers.description: Detailed evaluation of candidate seniority, project ownership history, trade-off reasoning, and team-specific mission fit.
barriers.pass_condition: Hiring manager confirms candidate has required depth and approves progression to final panel.

specimens.label: The question this gate is built around

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: Tell me about a decision on that project you would make differently now.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: We picked synchronous calls between two services because it was faster to ship. It cost us during incidents — a queue would have been the right call.

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: What made you choose speed at the time?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: A launch date we had committed to externally.

specimens.reading: This gate is testing ownership and trade-off reasoning, not knowledge. It is also the gate where an undisclosed house preference does the most damage.

barriers.title: Team & Cross-Functional Panel
barriers.content:
# Team & Cross-Functional Panel

Multi-interviewer round assessing collaborative problem solving, code review etiquette, cross-functional communication, and cultural norms.

### Pass Condition
Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.
barriers.description: Multi-interviewer round assessing collaborative problem solving, code review etiquette, cross-functional communication, and cultural norms.
barriers.pass_condition: Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.

specimens.label: Panel tally, as submitted

lines.text: Panelist 1 — collaboration 4, communication 4: hire
Panelist 2 — collaboration 4, communication 3: hire
Panelist 3 — collaboration 3, communication 2: no hire
Consensus threshold: unanimous, or manager override.
Outcome: not aligned.

specimens.reading: The gate is not an average, it is a veto rule. One dissent and a unanimity requirement produce the same result as three dissents.

barriers.title: Compensation & Leveling Reconciliation
barriers.content:
# Compensation & Leveling Reconciliation

Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / leveling grid.

### Pass Condition
Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.
barriers.description: Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / leveling grid.
barriers.pass_condition: Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.

specimens.label: Levelling reconciliation sheet

lines.text: Candidate expectation: 90k · Approved band for L4: 68–79k · Approved band for L5: 84–98k
Panel levelled the candidate at L4.
Gap: 11k above the top of the approved band. Options: level up (needs VP approval), reduce expectation, or close.

specimens.reading: Two independent decisions — a level and a band — meet here for the first time. Neither was visible to the candidate while they were being made.

barriers.title: Headcount & Executive Budget Approval
barriers.content:
# Headcount & Executive Budget Approval

Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.

### Pass Condition
Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.
barriers.description: Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.
barriers.pass_condition: Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.

specimens.label: Approval chain

lines.text: Hiring manager: approved
Director: approved
Finance: pending — quarterly review in progress
Talent committee: blocked on finance
Offer cannot be issued while any step is pending.

specimens.reading: Everyone the candidate met has already said yes. This gate is the reason a process can stop after a unanimous panel.

barriers.title: Reference & Background Verification
barriers.content:
# Reference & Background Verification

Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.

### Pass Condition
All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.
barriers.description: Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.
barriers.pass_condition: All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.

specimens.label: Verification report

lines.text: Employment record 1 of 3: dates confirmed
Employment record 2 of 3: vendor has Mar 2019–Jun 2021, application states Jan 2019–Aug 2021 — DISCREPANCY
Degree: confirmed · References: 2 of 2 returned, both positive
Offer held pending reconciliation.

specimens.reading: The gate is checking a third-party record against a claim. A mismatch here is usually a document problem with a named remedy, not a finding about honesty.

barriers.title: Offer Closing & Contract Execution
barriers.content:
# Offer Closing & Contract Execution

Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.

### Pass Condition
Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.
barriers.description: Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.
barriers.pass_condition: Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.

specimens.label: Closing sequence

lines.text: Contract issued for signature
Candidate signed
Countersignature pending
Start date confirmed · onboarding workflow triggered

specimens.reading: A signature from one side is not the gate. Until the countersignature lands the requisition is still open, which is where a late freeze can reach it.

mechanisms.title: Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
mechanisms.content:
# Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.
mechanisms.summary: The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

specimens.label: Feedback naming the gap
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical round

lines.text: The panel was positive on communication and on how you structured the problem.
The gap was concrete: the concurrency exercise needed a bounded worker pool and the submitted solution spawned unbounded goroutines, which the panel would expect to be caught at this level.
We would genuinely welcome a re-application once that area has had some time.

specimens.reading: A named exercise and a named property. This is the shape of feedback that is about the work rather than about fit — rare, and worth keeping.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.

mechanisms.title: Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort
mechanisms.content:
# Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

specimens.label: Rejection naming the comparison

lines.text: This was a genuinely difficult decision — you cleared every bar we set.
We went with another finalist who has shipped the same payment rails we are migrating to, which shortens the ramp by a quarter or so.
If anything opens at this level again I would like to come back to you directly.

specimens.reading: Nothing here says the candidate fell short. A comparison decided it, and comparisons are not properties of either person.

non_inferences: Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.

mechanisms.title: ATS Parser Extraction Failure
mechanisms.content:
# ATS Parser Extraction Failure

Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.
mechanisms.summary: Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

specimens.label: Parsed profile, as the ATS stored it
specimens.context: the same CV that renders correctly in a PDF reader

lines.text: Name: parsed · Email: parsed · Phone: parsed
Work experience: 0 entries
Skills: 0 entries
Raw text captured: 340 characters of a 4,100-character document
Ranking score: 12/100 — insufficient experience

specimens.reading: The document was not read and rejected; it was not read. A two-column layout and a graphic header are enough to produce this.

non_inferences: Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.

mechanisms.title: Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
mechanisms.content:
# Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-013` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

specimens.label: The number nobody published

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before the manager round — what were your expectations again?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: 85–95k, as I mentioned at the screen.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. I should be straight with you: the approved budget for this req tops out at 74k. It was never in the posting.

specimens.reading: The mismatch existed on day one and surfaced in week four. Four rounds were spent on a gap that a published band would have shown immediately.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.

mechanisms.title: Pre-Selected Internal Candidate
mechanisms.content:
# Pre-Selected Internal Candidate

Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-002` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.
mechanisms.summary: Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

specimens.label: Final round, an aside

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: How many people are you seeing for this?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: You are the third external. There is also someone internal who has been covering part of the scope since spring.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Is that a formal candidacy?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: It is. We post externally regardless — that is policy.

specimens.reading: Nothing improper is described. The posting is real, the process is real, and the odds were set before the first external application arrived.

non_inferences: Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.

mechanisms.title: Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
mechanisms.content:
# Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `void`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-020` — Automated Application Expiration Timeout

### Non-Inferences
- Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.
mechanisms.summary: Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

specimens.label: Asking whether the role is alive

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I applied for this in January and again in March — is the posting current?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Let me check. That team stopped hiring in December; the listing should have come down. I will get it removed.

specimens.reading: The posting was not bait and it was not a decision. It was a record nobody owned, which is a different thing to be angry at.

non_inferences: Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.

mechanisms.title: Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation
mechanisms.content:
# Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation

Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-006` — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
- Masks `M-002` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.
mechanisms.summary: Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

specimens.label: The freeze, as announced downward

lines.text: I have to pause our process. A hiring freeze was announced across the division this morning, effective immediately.
Your final round was scheduled for Thursday. I am cancelling it rather than having you prepare for something I cannot honour.
I will tell you plainly when I know anything, including if the answer is that this will not reopen.

specimens.reading: The cause is above the hiring loop and dated. Whether it is checkable against public news is the probe worth running.

non_inferences: Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.

mechanisms.title: Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter
mechanisms.content:
# Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-011` — Employment Gap Downranking Bias
- Amplifies `M-013` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition — over-filtering strong generalists prolongs the search until the team redefines the role mid-process; see loop L-003

### Non-Inferences
- Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.
mechanisms.summary: Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

specimens.label: Screening rules, as they ran

lines.text: Rule 1: must_contain("Kubernetes") — PASS
Rule 2: must_contain("CKA") — candidate holds CKAD — FAIL
Rule 3: not evaluated (short-circuit)
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: An adjacent certification is not a near miss to a string match; it is a miss. The filter compares tokens, not competence.

non_inferences: Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.

mechanisms.title: Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion
mechanisms.content:
# Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

Recruiters optimize for pipeline velocity and superficial pattern-matching due to overwhelming applicant volume (500+ per req).

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-012` — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
- Masks `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean recruiter is individually negligent; reflects structural capacity mismatch.
mechanisms.summary: Recruiters optimize for pipeline velocity and superficial pattern-matching due to overwhelming applicant volume (500+ per req).

specimens.label: The queue the screen ran against

lines.text: Applications received: 640
Recruiter screening capacity this week: 40
Median time spent per profile: 7 seconds
Profiles advanced: 11

specimens.reading: Seven seconds is not a judgement of a career. It is what a queue of 640 does to attention, whoever is holding it.

non_inferences: Does not mean recruiter is individually negligent; reflects structural capacity mismatch.

mechanisms.title: Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority
mechanisms.content:
# Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority

The interview team grades candidate against specific undisclosed architectural dogmas, internal frameworks, or unwritten biases.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-022` — Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Failure to guess unstated preferences is not equivalent to lack of core competence.
mechanisms.summary: The interview team grades candidate against specific undisclosed architectural dogmas, internal frameworks, or unwritten biases.

specimens.label: The rubric that was not in the brief

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I would put a queue between them so the write path stays available if the consumer is down.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Mm. We do not use queues here.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is that a constraint I should design within?

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Just carry on.

specimens.reading: A house preference was applied as a grading criterion without being stated as one. The candidate could not have designed to a rule they were not told.

non_inferences: Failure to guess unstated preferences is not equivalent to lack of core competence.

mechanisms.title: Employment Gap Downranking Bias
mechanisms.content:
# Employment Gap Downranking Bias

Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Employment gap does not correlate with underlying technical decline.
mechanisms.summary: Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

specimens.label: Ranking breakdown, as scored

lines.text: Skills match: 91/100
Domain match: 88/100
Continuity penalty: −22 (gap of 14 months detected)
Final rank: 57/100 — below advance threshold

specimens.reading: The penalty is applied to a date range, not to anything in the work. Nothing the candidate shipped during or after the gap is in the arithmetic.

non_inferences: Employment gap does not correlate with underlying technical decline.

mechanisms.title: Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
mechanisms.content:
# Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation

Engineering interviewers are overwhelmed with sprint commitments, leading to calendar fragmentation, rush reviews, or dropped loops.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-019` — Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

### Non-Inferences
- Rescheduling is an operational issue and does not indicate negative evaluation.
mechanisms.summary: Engineering interviewers are overwhelmed with sprint commitments, leading to calendar fragmentation, rush reviews, or dropped loops.

specimens.label: Inside the interviewer calendar

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Can you take the panel Thursday? Nobody else on the team is free.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I am on release duty and I have not read the take-home. I can do it but it will be a cold read.

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Take it. We are already two weeks over on this req.

specimens.reading: The evaluation was compromised before it began, and nothing in the candidate could have changed that. This trace lives on the other side of the table.

non_inferences: Rescheduling is an operational issue and does not indicate negative evaluation.

mechanisms.title: Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
mechanisms.content:
# Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition

Team changes tech stack, seniority requirements, or project scope mid-funnel, invalidating previous interview assessments.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-004` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
- Amplifies `M-024` — Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs — each redefinition re-inflates the requisition with new must-haves instead of trimming it; see loop L-003
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Candidate rejection was driven by shifting team mandate, not prior interview answers.
mechanisms.summary: Team changes tech stack, seniority requirements, or project scope mid-funnel, invalidating previous interview assessments.

specimens.label: The role that changed underneath

lines.text: Thank you for the four rounds — the panel notes were strong throughout.

Since we opened this req the team has moved the service to Rust and folded the on-call leadership into the role. Weighted against the new profile we are looking for someone with production Rust and formal lead experience.
I recognise you interviewed against the previous description. I am sorry about that.

specimens.reading: The assessments were not re-run, they were re-scored against a target that moved after they were taken.

non_inferences: Candidate rejection was driven by shifting team mandate, not prior interview answers.

mechanisms.title: Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint
mechanisms.content:
# Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint
